matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When attempting to fix the equation, first try moving a single matchstick within the same character to turn it into another valid Roman numeral, before considering moves that involve different characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation is invalid and any character consists of multiple sticks (e.g., V, X, L).
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from V and moving it to another character, which leaves V as a single diagonal (invalid) instead of repositioning it within V to become X.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, verify that each resulting character matches a recognized Roman numeral or allowed operator; discard any move that produces an unknown shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before any arithmetic check.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X and leaving X as a single diagonal line, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not correspond to any Roman numeral; ensure that removing a diagonal from a character that originally had two diagonals (V or X) does not leave a single diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When taking a diagonal from a V or X.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from V and moving it elsewhere, leaving V as a lone diagonal stick.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equation, explore moving a stick from one character to a different character, ensuring both source and destination remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character possibilities without success.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical part of '+' to another numeral but forgetting to check that '+' remains a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation after any transformation; the equality must hold in Roman numeral arithmetic.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After a candidate move passes symbol validation.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformation that makes the left side 15 and the right side 12 without checking the mismatch.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If a stick is taken from the '=' sign, ensure the remaining symbol still forms a valid equality sign (i.e., at least one horizontal line) and that exactly one '=' remains in the final equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick from the equality operator.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from '=', leaving no '=' sign in the equation.

matchstick.title: Validate whole numeral strings for proper Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: After the move, check that each multi‑character numeral follows standard Roman numeral ordering rules (e.g., no illegal repetitions, correct subtractive patterns).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After symbol validation and before arithmetic check.
matchstick.example: Creating 'IXIV' by moving a stick, which violates Roman numeral syntax.

matchstick.title: Intra-character diagonal transformation (V↔X)
matchstick.principle: When a character is V or X (both made of two diagonal sticks), moving one diagonal within the same character can change V into X or X into V; this single‑stick move often resolves the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation contains a V or X and no intra‑character move has yet succeeded, try repositioning one of its diagonals to form the other shape.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal from V and moving it to a different character, leaving V as a single diagonal, instead of repositioning it within V to become X.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model jumps to moving sticks between characters, missing simple shape changes that stay within a single character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always attempt intra‑character relocations first; check if a character can become another valid numeral by moving one of its own sticks.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: Removing a diagonal from a two‑diagonal character leaves an unsupported shape that does not correspond to any Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never leave a character with only one diagonal; if a diagonal is removed, ensure the character still matches a known numeral (e.g., V↔X transformation).

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on symbol validity and forgets to check whether the resulting equation is numerically correct.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any move that passes symbol checks, immediately compute the values of both sides and confirm equality.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats operator changes as free fixes, overlooking the requirement that exactly one equality sign must stay in the final equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When altering an operator, verify that the equality sign is still present exactly once and that the new operator is valid in the context.

matchstick.description: Creating nonstandard Roman numeral forms (e.g., IXIV) that are not valid according to standard Roman numeral rules
matchstick.why_it_happens: Stick moves can produce illegal numeral sequences that the model does not recognize as invalid.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After symbol validation, run a Roman‑numeral syntax check on each multi‑character numeral before evaluating arithmetic.
